briefing.headline: OpenAI o4 and DeepSeek R2 escalate frontier race as US export controls tighten

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: Frontier labs released multiple reasoning upgrades this week while governments accelerated export controls. Compute demand continues to outstrip supply with major sovereign AI projects advancing in parallel.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI deployed o4-preview with 4x multi-agent coordination gains. DeepSeek open-sourced R2-70B matching o3 performance on coding benchmarks. Anthropic and Google DeepMind both teased next-generation multimodal agents expected within 60 days.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems. DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level with successful automotive CAN bus and multi-agent pilots reported this week.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: TSMC began volume production of 2nm AI chips for NVIDIA and Broadcom. Microsoft and CoreWeave announced $4B joint data center expansion across three new US sites with liquid cooling at scale.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will export controls on advanced AI chips meaningfully slow Chinese frontier progress or simply accelerate domestic alternatives?
